title: Prepared Transaction Remediation Architecture Audit after F-VQ60
scope: Owner remediation of F-VQ60 B1 revision overflow and B2 copied prepared-handle replay, plus current-canonical reconciliation. This audit is not independent qualification and is not canonical admission.

invariants.assessment: One shared groundwater-exchange contract is added; no use-case-specific SWAP kernel is introduced.
The runtime contract contains no file, path, parser, file-unit or legacy-format dependency.
Checkpoint, candidate, prepared reservation and trial result remain explicit transaction data rather than being mixed with forcing or immutable parameters.
Only preparable services allocate reservation-registry state. Storage scales with peak concurrent prepared reservations and is reused; no permanent state is added per logical SWAP column.
No Newton vectors, Jacobians or constitutive scratch are added to persistent column state.
Reservation slots are pooled and reusable. A free-list gives O(1) reserve/release operations with geometric growth, leaving batched or SoA column storage unconstrained.
Prepare does not publish committed groundwater state. Commit and abort consume an exact wrapper-owned slot generation before backend entry, so stale copied handles cannot mutate committed state.
Abort releases a reservation without physical publication and leaves the originating checkpoint reusable; failed or stale trials do not replace committed state.
The contract uses generic coupling-window times and introduces no day, month, year or midnight assumption.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced; the existing generic t0/t1 window contract is preserved.
Transactional groundwater prepare, commit and abort behavior is explicit runtime functionality, including fail-closed replay protection.
Head/flux interface conventions and groundwater lineage provenance are not altered. Revision provenance now fails closed when no int64 successor exists.
No mass tolerance is relaxed. Preventing replayed prepared commits specifically prevents duplicate groundwater publication from copied handles.
No interface-sensitivity or response-tangent contract is removed or constrained.
The remediation adds no extra SWAP predictor/corrector trajectories; reservation checks are local metadata operations.
MultiSWAP remains primary: no heavy solver instance is added per column, registry memory is O(peak concurrent reservations), reserve/release is O(1) apart from amortized geometric growth.
No one-to-one relationship between a SWAP column and a MODFLOW cell is introduced.
Deep-vadose transfer ownership and behavior are untouched.
No component-transition storage or accounting rule is changed; duplicate prepared publication is prevented.
The groundwater transaction contract is independent of the selected soil-water solver implementation.
No crop, ET, drainage, irrigation or surface-process implementation is duplicated or specialized.
No HeadCalc internal array or numerical implementation detail is exposed.
The change is transaction safety/runtime policy only and does not silently alter physical options.
No unbounded retry path is added. Revision exhaustion and stale prepared handles fail closed; reservation lookup is O(1) and growth is geometric.
Reference-mode physics and numerical behavior are unchanged.
Explicit statuses identify stale prepared handles, exhausted revisions and unavailable reservation storage; transaction outcomes remain diagnosable.
Reservation storage exists only on the opt-in preparable subtype and is lazily allocated, so non-preparable services pay no registry memory cost.
System composition remains outside the SWAP kernel. Runtime ownership must serialize mutations of one preparable-service instance; this is explicit rather than silently assumed.
No file, calendar, MODFLOW or run-start assumption is introduced. Revision headroom and reservation identity are checked explicitly.
This remediation is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP architecture invariants; independent qualification remains a separate required gate.

hard_nonclaims: This owner audit is not independent F-VQ qualification.
This owner audit does not admit GC18 or GC18R into integration/f-ci-canonical.
This remediation does not claim a full MultiSWAP throughput benchmark; it removes the avoidable linear reservation-slot scan and preserves scalable ownership semantics.
This remediation does not change groundwater physics, mass tolerances or interface sign conventions.
